questions.topic: Many significant subgroups and one of them
questions.learningObjective: Explain the garden-of-forking-paths risk in subgroup hunting
questions.stem: Why is searching many subgroups for significance called a garden of forking paths?

answer.exemplar: Each choice of subgroup, cutoff, or outcome creates another path, and only significant results get reported, inflating false positives and making chance findings look real.

questions.explanation: Many analytic choices create paths, and selective reporting inflates false positives.
questions.hint: Many choices create paths and selective reporting inflates errors.

options.text: Larger sample sizes automatically
options.misconception: correction does not change sample size

questions.learningObjective: Compute the corrected per-test alpha for six tests
questions.stem: To keep family-wise alpha at 0.05 across 6 tests, what Bonferroni per-test alpha is needed?

questions.learningObjective: Compute reliability of an average of five ratings
questions.stem: A single rating has reliability 0.50; what is the reliability of the average of five ratings?
questions.explanation: 5 times 0.50 over 1 plus 4 times 0.50 equals 0.8333. More raters help with diminishing returns.
